trust_decision.summary: Nothing decides who may invoke tools over the self-hosted HTTP transport: the Express app is built for host '0.0.0.0' (which turns the SDK's host-header/rebinding check off) and POST/GET/DELETE /mcp are mounted with no authorization check, so any client that reaches the port can initialize a session and spend the operator's DEEPSEEK_API_KEY; the decision has to be made in the /mcp middleware of createHttpApp plus the env-config seam that supplies the token and the bind host.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'Missing Authentication on Self-Hosted HTTP MCP Endpoint', so an engineer opens the only HTTP transport module and finds createHttpApp building the app for 0.0.0.0 at src/transport-http.ts:17 with three unguarded /mcp handlers (src/transport-http.ts:31, 72, 86); README.md:547-560 documents the same self-hosted path as `TRANSPORT=http ... node dist/index.js` -> POST /mcp.

fix_sites.entry_point: loadConfig()/getConfig() consumed by the bin entry (src/index.ts:23,34)
main() HTTP branch, i.e. `node dist/index.js` with TRANSPORT=http
startHttpTransport() exported server bootstrap (the only app.listen)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: config.ts contains no HTTP handler, so an engineer can call it plain environment plumbing that is 'the transport's business' and leave it alone - after which HTTP_AUTH_TOKEN and HTTP_HOST can never reach the app and the shipped CLI stays open while the unit-level fixes look complete.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Every path other than /mcp must stay reachable without credentials: the container HEALTHCHECK probes GET /health every 30s, and the stdio transport has no network surface and must not start demanding a token; an app-wide auth middleware or a token check placed in the tool layer breaks both.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: Dockerfile:18-19 (health probe) and src/index.ts:86-89 (stdio branch); the second constraint is already encoded at src/transport-http.test.ts:49-67, where POST /mcp initialize expects 200 with no Authorization header.

O6_input_shapes: Authorization: Bearer <token> present and correct on /mcp -> 200
Authorization header present with a wrong token -> 401
HTTP_AUTH_TOKEN unset -> /mcp deliberately stays open (existing single-tenant deployments)
HTTP_HOST = '0.0.0.0' or '::' with no token -> startup warning, endpoint not closed
HTTP_ALLOWED_HOSTS = CSV with spaces and a trailing empty element -> trimmed, empties dropped
methods POST (session create), GET (SSE stream) and DELETE (session terminate) all on /mcp

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Legacy MCP HTTP+SSE routes (GET /sse + POST /messages) mounted next to /mcp
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The SDK still ships the older SSE transport beside StreamableHTTP, and a maintainer keeping older clients working would mount those routes at the app root; the published guard is path-scoped (app.use('/mcp', ...)), so the same unauthenticated tool-invocation sink would sit outside it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A shared-instance gateway token on the Cloudflare Worker's /mcp in addition to the BYOK bearer
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The worker already gates /mcp on the request's own bearer and has an empty Env interface, so adding a secret-backed token for rate-limiting or abuse control on a shared deployment is a one-line extension a maintainer could plausibly write.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An alternative credential for /mcp (?api_key= query param or X-Api-Key header) beside the Authorization check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Clients that cannot set an Authorization header are common enough that self-hosted servers add a query/header fallback; that weaker path would bypass the constant-time bearer comparison entirely.

O9_family: authentication/authorization - missing authentication for a critical function (CWE-306) on a network-exposed MCP endpoint

O10_build.toolchain: Node >=18 at the pinned commit (engines + CI matrix 18/20/22), npm ci + tsc (npm run build), vitest 4 for tests
O10_build.project_tests: src/transport-http.test.ts (createHttpApp: /health 200, POST /mcp 200/400, GET+DELETE /mcp 400), src/transport-isolation.test.ts (per-session SessionStore), src/config.test.ts (env parsing); the fix's src/transport-auth.test.ts does not exist at the pinned commit. The auth tests bind a loopback port and make no outbound calls, so the affected behaviour runs offline; the build itself needs npm registry access for npm ci.

j.j_sites_touched: src/config.ts, src/index.ts, src/transport-http.ts (src/server.ts is a version-literal bump only)
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add an auth middleware in createHttpApp that reads process.env.HTTP_AUTH_TOKEN directly (or guard only the POST handler), stop there, and never touch the config schema/loader, startHttpTransport or the bind host.

out_of_scope_notes: worker/src/index.ts:353 is a second HTTP MCP implementation in a separate deployable (Cloudflare Worker, wrangler.toml route); it authenticates with the caller's own DeepSeek key (extractApiKey at worker/src/index.ts:25-29, empty Env) and holds no server credential, so it is outside this advisory's protection and was not pursued.

Dockerfile:12 and docker-compose.yml publish port 3000 with TRANSPORT=http and no token before the fix; deployment-level exposure is config/docs, covered by the same advisory, noted here rather than analysed.
